Herd.et: From Middle High German hërt, from Old High German hërd, from Proto-West Germanic *herþ. Cognate with Dutch haard, English hearth.

s: herd, flock (group of livestock or other large mammals)
Herde.et:
From Middle High German hërt, from Old High German hërta, from Proto-West Germanic *herdu.
The modern consonantism is Central and Low German (compare Middle Low German hērde). Cognate with English herd, Danish hjord, Swedish hjord, Gothic 𐌷𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌳𐌰 (hairda).

s: a surname
hearth (or more literally, the fire therein; particularly as a place around which the family gathers)
Am Herdfeuer erzählten sich unsere Vorfahren die alten Märchen.
At the hearth, our ancestors told the old folktales.
synonym of Betreuungsgeld (a bonus incentive for parents to remain at home)
colloquial
derogatory
Herdprämie.et: Herd (“cooker”) + Prämie (“bonus”), evoking Heimchen am Herd.
